documentation.title: Introduction to Firebase Local Emulator Suite
Install, configure and integrate Local Emulator Suite

baseline.upgradePolicy: Bumping the pin in conformance/package.json and re-recording turns every newly detected difference into a debt row in conformance/DEBT.md, because a row can only become a documented divergence once a human writes it into conformance/divergences.json. Any surface the new baseline adds is absent from this contract, so compat-check fails until it is enumerated with a scope; until then the claim sentence names the old version and is therefore false, which is the intended fail-closed behaviour.

claim.sentence: fireemu is compatible with the listed Local Emulator Suite products as shipped by firebase-tools 15.28.2 -- Cloud Firestore, Firebase Authentication, Cloud Storage for Firebase, Cloud Functions, Cloud Pub/Sub and Eventarc, with Security Rules on the Firestore and Storage surfaces -- under the `firebase` compatibility profile and the evidence recorded in `spec/compatibility/contract.json`; it makes no complete-suite and no unqualified superset claim while Realtime Database, Firebase Hosting, App Hosting and Data Connect are deferred and Firebase Extensions is not planned.
claim.rule: The claim is version-qualified and product-enumerated. It may not be widened to a complete-suite or unqualified superset claim while any surface in this contract has scope deferred or not-planned. The documents under scopedDocuments (what a release ships as its description) are held to the same scope rule as the README: a deferred or not-planned product may be named there only with its scope disclaimer.

firebase.intent: Reproduce the behaviour the pinned Local Emulator Suite ships and Firebase documents, including its documented limitations. fireemu may not add a rejection in this profile: extra strictness belongs to the strict profile.

limits.enforcement.note: the limits section is schema-validated; neutral observe is accepted as metadata, while strict enforcement is rejected as not implemented. The Standard query limits are switched by firestore.enforceLimits, which the profile derives

limits.quotaAccounting.note: neutral off is accepted as metadata; observe and enforce are rejected as not implemented and no quota is accounted

limits.warningsAsErrors.note: the neutral empty list is accepted as metadata; non-empty warning promotion is rejected as not implemented

rules.staticLimitChecks.note: accepted by the loader and read by nothing; the compile-time call-graph limits are official behaviour (RULES-PARITY-03) and are always on

rules.runtimeBudgets.note: accepted by the loader and read by nothing; the document-access budgets are official behaviour (RULES-PARITY-03) and are always on

auth.idTokenSigning.note: read by the loader, defaulting to unsigned-emulator whatever the profile; strict has to name session-rsa itself

appCheck.enabled.note: read by the loader, defaulting to false whatever the profile; enabling App Check needs the apps registered next to it, so a profile could not switch it on alone

events.delivery.note: the loader refuses every value but exactly-once-test

scheduler.clock.note: the loader refuses every value but virtual

projects.requireDemoPrefix.note: read by the loader; the runtime default stays true in both profiles on purpose, because that guard is what stops a run from reaching a real project by accident -- the firebase profile declares false only to record what the official CLI does

officialEmulatorDivergences.note: The pinned official Firestore emulator does not check composite indexes at all, so the profile that reproduces it assumes every index a query needs and reports each assumption as FS_EMULATOR_INDEX_ASSUMED. The firebase value reproduces the Firebase backend instead, which refuses the same query; a run whose oracle is production rather than the emulator sets it explicitly. Both values are official behaviour of a different oracle; conservative is neither and belongs to the strict profile.

officialEmulatorDivergences.profileValue: unsigned mock tokens are admitted, with the audience still bound to the routed Firestore resource project or Storage bucket project and a signed token still verified
officialEmulatorDivergences.emulatorValue: no verification at all: the token is decoded and request.auth is built from whatever it carries
officialEmulatorDivergences.note: Measured against the pinned suite on 2026-08-31 with an unsigned token whose sub names no user: the Firestore emulator admitted it, admitted an exp of 3600 seconds after the epoch, admitted a token with no exp and no iss, admitted one whose aud named another project, and admitted one whose RS256 signature was garbage; the Storage emulator behaves the same way by construction (firebase-tools/lib/emulator/storage/rules/runtime.js calls jwt.decode). The firebase profile reproduces the part @firebase/rules-unit-testing depends on -- an unsigned token for an unknown subject with an expiry nobody reads -- and keeps two checks the official emulators skip: the audience must name the routed Firestore resource project or Storage bucket project, so a token cannot cross a session or project boundary, and a signed token must still verify, so a forged RS256 token never becomes an identity. An unregistered Firestore project owned by the default session is a valid routed namespace and is not replaced by the configured Auth project for this comparison. Both checks are refusals of requests the official emulator admits, which is why they are recorded here rather than left implicit.

officialEmulatorDivergences.profileValue: email action codes expire after 3600 s and phone verification codes after 600 s of virtual time, pending second-factor sign-ins after 3600 s, a TOTP enrollment session answers SESSION_EXPIRED for one further session lifetime and is then reaped, and each kind refuses with QUOTA_EXCEEDED past 1000 outstanding codes per project or 32 pending sessions per user; expired entries are swept before every request and never observable
officialEmulatorDivergences.emulatorValue: no expiry and no budget: every code stays until it is consumed and the pending credential is a stateless base64 document (firebase-tools/lib/emulator/auth/state.js createOob, createVerificationCode; operations.js mfaPending)
officialEmulatorDivergences.note: Read from the pinned source rather than measured with a clock: the official emulator has no virtual clock to advance past a lifetime. fireemu bounds the retained state so abandoned flows cannot grow a session without limit (INV-AUTH-004); every in-window credential keeps its one-time consumption semantics, and refresh tokens are not part of the policy. Documented in README.md, "Authentication".

officialEmulatorDivergences.profileValue: the 324-row Firestore semantics matrix (conformance/firestore-matrix.json), with 118 rows pinned to fireemu's own answer and authority in conformance/divergences.json
officialEmulatorDivergences.emulatorValue: the same rows as the official emulator records them
officialEmulatorDivergences.note: Measured against the pinned suite over the REST surface both emulators serve (authority checked 2026-09-06). The pinned divergence rows fall into five families, each backed by a production observation in conformance/firestore-production-matrix.json where production could serve the row: (1) production's REST wire shape -- no `done` marker on the last runQuery or runAggregationQuery element, a leading readTime/skippedResults element for an offset, no nextPageToken on a page that holds the last results, batchGet answered found-first in name order -- where the official emulator differs; (2) production's validation codes -- a second array-contains filter, a read_time before database creation, committing a read-only transaction and more than 500 field transforms on one document are INVALID_ARGUMENT -- where the official emulator answers FAILED_PRECONDITION or accepts; (3) official REST-adapter defects fireemu does not reproduce -- a bytes-typed query parameter (?transaction=) hangs the connection without a response, ?readTime= misparses (a read at the latest commit time included), a malformed page token and a fileless :securityRules body answer HTTP 500; (4) an official leniency fireemu refuses -- a write addressed to another database than the route; (5) capabilities fireemu serves that the official emulator refuses -- orderBy(__name__, desc) and PartitionQuery. Transactions lock what they read on both emulators and in production, so the transaction-concurrency rows are parity. Everything else in the matrix is parity, gated on status, canonical code and normalized body.

strict.intent: Add fireemu's stricter validation on top of the firebase profile. Every key here may only refuse more than the official emulator, never less, and every refusal it adds must be published as a capability precision or a documented divergence.

limits.enforcement.note: strict enforcement is rejected as not implemented; neutral limits metadata is schema-validated and the Standard query limits are switched by firestore.enforceLimits, which the profile derives

limits.quotaAccounting.note: observe accounting is rejected as not implemented; neutral off is accepted as metadata and no quota is accounted

rules.staticLimitChecks.note: accepted by the loader and read by nothing; the compile-time call-graph limits are official behaviour (RULES-PARITY-03) and are always on

rules.runtimeBudgets.note: accepted by the loader and read by nothing; the document-access budgets are official behaviour (RULES-PARITY-03) and are always on

auth.idTokenSigning.note: read by the loader, defaulting to unsigned-emulator whatever the profile; strict has to name session-rsa itself

appCheck.enabled.note: read by the loader, defaulting to false whatever the profile; enabling App Check needs the apps registered next to it, so a profile could not switch it on alone

events.delivery.note: the only value the loader accepts, so the default already

scheduler.clock.note: the only value the loader accepts, so the default already

projects.requireDemoPrefix.note: read by the loader; the runtime default stays true in both profiles on purpose, because that guard is what stops a run from reaching a real project by accident -- the firebase profile declares false only to record what the official CLI does

profileStatus: The profile is a runtime switch, and its sets list exactly what the daemon derives from it: firestore.indexValidationPolicy (emulator / conservative) and firestore.enforceLimits (a Standard query limit violation is reported as an FS_LIMIT_OBSERVED warning / refuses the query). Two further derived settings have no configuration key: how a caller's ID token is verified on the Firestore and Storage Security Rules surfaces (the official emulators' unsigned mock tokens are admitted / the full verification against the Auth store stands), and whether Auth refresh tokens remain stateless like the official emulator or are revoked after privileged account mutations. An explicit configuration key always wins over the profile's default for it. A unit test in crates/fireemu/src/config.rs reads this file and fails when a profile's sets and what set_profile derives disagree. Every other key a profile names is under declared, with a status: hand-written means the loader reads the key but does not derive it from the profile, not-implemented means the loader refuses the value or reads nothing of the section, so the value is a statement of intent and not a switch. fireemu capabilities and GET /v1/capabilities publish the active profile and the start banner prints it. tools/compat-check CC-08 checks every key and value under sets and declared against spec/config/fireemu.schema.json, requires a status and a note on each declared key, refuses a key that is both set and declared, and checks that the profile names declared here are exactly the values that schema's profile key accepts.

scopes.active: In the supported-surface milestone. Either parity is claimed with evidence, the surface is a fireemu addition, or it is an open gap that blocks the complete-suite claim.
scopes.deferred: In the pinned baseline, deliberately not implemented for now. Blocks any complete-suite or unqualified superset claim.
scopes.not-planned: In the pinned baseline, deliberately never implemented. Blocks any complete-suite claim against this baseline.

states.claimed: parity is claimed against the pinned official emulator, with executed evidence
states.addition: a fireemu surface with no official counterpart; never described as parity
states.gap: an active surface with no parity claim yet

sharedTerms.qualifier: validation-only: a well-formed pipeline is answered UNIMPLEMENTED FS_PIPE_VALIDATION_ONLY
Storage object finalized / deleted / metadataUpdated events reach v1 and v2 handlers
limitedUse: true fails closed with 501 APP_CHECK_REPLAY_UNSUPPORTED

surfaces.title: Cloud Firestore
surfaces.decision: Active supported surface. Parity is claimed for the gRPC service, the REST API, the WebChannel transport and Security Rules, against the pinned official emulator.

claims.statement: The Firestore v1 gRPC service serves documents, atomic commits, serializable transactions, queries, aggregations and the Write and Listen streams against local state, with the same status codes and error shapes as the pinned official emulator except for the rows pinned in conformance/divergences.json, where fireemu follows a recorded production observation instead; transactions lock what they read, as production and the official Local Emulator Suite both do. A committed server timestamp is immediately available to a transaction query, including a combined equality and timestamp-range filter with limit(1). Removing and replacing a listener target never delivers the removed target's changes, replacing a WebChannel backchannel cancels the superseded response before it can deliver queued arrays, and a long-poll response remains attached until its HTTP body reaches EOF or is dropped.
officialLimitations: the official Firestore emulator holds every database in memory and loses it on exit unless the run exports it, so no fixture may assume durable state

measured by the semantics matrix: the official Firestore emulator does enforce the per-value byte cap (1,048,487 bytes), the nesting depth of 20, the 1,500-byte field-name and document-id caps, at most 30 IN values and a single array-contains clause; it does not enforce the 500-transforms-per-document budget or any composite index, so the firebase profile observes those instead of refusing them

fireemuOnly.behaviour: a one-hour read_time retention window with exact resume replay recomputed from retained MVCC history, and an ExistenceFilter carrying the exact count rather than a bloom filter
seeded fault injection on firestore.commit / read / beginTransaction

productionOnly: real index build latency and backfill

claims.statement: The Firestore REST API is served on the Firestore port next to gRPC and reproduces the official emulator's Google JSON error envelopes, including the firestore/lite transport.

excludedSteps.reason: status and canonical code agree; the message differs (the official emulator says "Payload isn't valid for request.", fireemu names the unknown operator)
status and canonical code agree; the word order of the message differs

the decision and the canonical code agree; only the denial message differs: the official emulator prints its per-allow evaluation trace, fireemu names the operation and the path and publishes the trace through its rules request-trace routes instead

officialLimitations: the official emulator refuses readTime selectors and findNearest on the REST surface rather than answering them

fireemuOnly.behaviour: Eventarc trigger definitions are limited to 256 KiB after project substitution, the live registry to 4096 entries and 16 MiB, one publish to 256 input events and 256 expanded deliveries, and the Functions runtime to 4096 active event records and 64 MiB of serialized payload and routing data; Eventarc may consume at most 3072 records and 48 MiB so other trigger sources retain a reservation, and admission fails atomically with 400, 413 or 429 rather than retaining unbounded local work

custom channels are bound to the registration project and compared as full resource names; non-loopback browser origins are refused and CORS is exposed only on the two google routes, preventing another local or remote project from driving trigger management or delivery through suffix matching

removal compares the semantic eventTrigger object rather than depending on JSON member insertion order, and a successful source reload rebuilds the manifest-owned table at the new generation instead of retaining manually duplicated stale-generation registrations

claims.statement: The browser web SDK's WebChannel v8 transport is served on the Firestore port, and a target refused on its own merits is removed without closing the channel. Unacknowledged arrays remain replayable by their original AIDs while explicit local byte budgets bound retained data, each response batch, and concurrently owned replay copies per session and per Hub.

fireemuOnly.behaviour: a target removed with its own cause (a missing composite index, a malformed query, a Rules denial) while the channel keeps serving its other targets

local memory-safety limits of 2 MiB per outbound array, 16 MiB of unacknowledged arrays per session, 4 MiB per framed backchannel batch, 4 MiB of concurrently owned replay copies per session, 64 MiB of unacknowledged arrays per Hub and 16 MiB of replay copies per Hub; overflow closes only the affected channel without weakening Security Rules

claims.statement: Composite index validation is a declared policy, not a hidden default: the emulator value reproduces the pinned official emulator, which serves a query whose composite index is not configured.
officialLimitations: the official Firestore emulator never checks composite indexes and serves the query as if the index existed; firestore.indexValidationPolicy = emulator is the value that reproduces it, and the FS_EMULATOR_INDEX_ASSUMED warning is fireemu-only

fireemuOnly.behaviour: firestore.indexValidationPolicy = conservative rejects a query whose composite index is not configured and prints the firestore.indexes.json fragment production would need

claims.statement: Production Firestore limits are versioned catalog entries with a disposition, so a limit violation is reported locally instead of surfacing only in production.
officialLimitations: the official emulator enforces a subset of the production limits (document bytes via the per-value cap, nesting depth, identifier lengths, IN values, array-contains count) and not the rest (transforms per document, composite indexes, transaction budgets are unmeasured); the firebase profile refuses exactly the measured subset and observes the production-only limits as warnings

fireemuOnly.behaviour: boundary-exact limit catalogs with a per-limit disposition and warning thresholds

productionOnly: quota, throughput and per-project rate limits

claims.statement: Security Rules are evaluated natively on every Firestore surface -- reads against the returned snapshot, writes inside the commit, queries proven from their constraints -- and on Firebase Storage requests, while the shared language is measured against the pinned official runtime rather than assumed.

excludedSteps.reason: the decision and the canonical code agree; only the denial message differs: the official emulator prints its per-allow evaluation trace, fireemu names the operation and the path and publishes the trace through its rules request-trace routes instead

the decision and the canonical code agree; only the denial message differs: the official emulator prints its per-allow evaluation trace, fireemu names the operation and the path and publishes the trace through its rules request-trace routes instead

the decision and the canonical code agree; only the denial message differs: the official emulator prints its per-allow evaluation trace, fireemu names the operation and the path and publishes the trace through its rules request-trace routes instead

the decision and the canonical code agree; only the denial message differs: the official emulator prints its per-allow evaluation trace, fireemu names the operation and the path and publishes the trace through its rules request-trace routes instead

officialLimitations: the official compiler's static type checker rejects three of the 680 recorded language claims while it compiles the file, where fireemu raises on them at evaluation; the request decision is the same in both and each row is pinned in conformance/rules-matrix.json

the official emulator answers a denial with a per-allow trace of its own evaluation; that text is a diagnostic rather than an API contract, so fireemu answers with its own message and publishes the same information through :ruleCoverage and the request-trace control route

fireemuOnly.behaviour: query proofs are sound but not complete: a rule that reads an unconstrained field denies the query rather than admitting it
static rules linting beyond what the official compiler reports, and runtime expression budgets

claims.statement: ExecutePipeline is decoded, identified and validated against the documented stage registry; a well-formed pipeline is answered UNIMPLEMENTED FS_PIPE_VALIDATION_ONLY rather than executed, and an unknown stage is refused rather than skipped.

fireemuOnly.behaviour: strict decode-and-validate with a canonical form in the refusal

preview: ExecutePipeline / StructuredPipeline is a preview Firestore surface; the pinned official emulator does not serve it either, so there is no oracle for its execution semantics

claims.statement: Firestore Enterprise text index definitions are validated at start and through the control API; the backfill lifecycle and local search are not served.

fireemuOnly.behaviour: duplicate index shapes are warned and unknown or output-only fields refused

preview: Firestore Enterprise edition and its text search surface are preview; the pinned official emulator ships no equivalent, so this claim is scoped to definition validation only

claims.statement: Rules evaluation is observable the way the official emulator makes it observable: the ruleset is loaded through :securityRules, and :ruleCoverage and :ruleCoverage.html report every expression by its source position with the values it took.
officialLimitations: the official report's `undefined` values name a zero-width position for the cause of some errors; fireemu names the extent of the innermost expression that raised, which is the same information at a position a reader can select

fireemuOnly.behaviour: GET /v1/sessions/{session}/rules/requests on the control API: the last 100 decided requests with their per-expression traces, behind the control token

surfaces.title: Firebase Authentication
surfaces.decision: Active supported surface. Parity is claimed for the Identity Toolkit subset the official emulator serves, including multi-factor enrolment and sign-in and synchronous beforeCreate and beforeSignIn Blocking Functions.
gaps: raw inbound OAuth credentials reach beforeCreate and beforeSignIn handlers only when auth.forwardInboundCredentials is enabled (default off) and only the token kinds the function's options request; the default emulator accepts the provider assertion and exposes its normalized claims, and the raw material is never retained in snapshots or exports. The per-token-kind matrix against real Node SDK handlers and the production expectation are still open in the Authentication parent issue
Android, Apple and Unity SDK matrices are outside the current Node/Web/REST/gRPC compatibility scope

claims.statement: The Identity Toolkit REST subset the Auth emulator serves is reproduced with the official error envelopes, including the Admin account routes real projects use (create, lookup, update, batchGet, batchCreate, batchDelete, query, session cookies, link generators), the client account routes (sign-up, sign-in, update, delete) and the emulator-only routes that read out-of-band codes and verification codes and read or change the project configuration. An unpinned daemon advances Auth request time monotonically, so a self-service credential change in a later second invalidates an earlier session cookie through validSince just as the Admin SDK observes on the official emulator.
officialLimitations: the official Auth emulator mails and texts nothing: codes are read from /emulator/v1/projects/{p}/oobCodes and verificationCodes
the official Auth emulator accepts reCAPTCHA tokens unchecked
the official Auth emulator performs no OAuth round trip: accounts:signInWithIdp trusts the assertion in postBody
the official Auth emulator's passwords are reversible (fakeHash:salt=...:password=...): an imported hash of any other algorithm never verifies, so such an account cannot sign in on either side

the official Auth emulator distinguishes EMAIL_NOT_FOUND from INVALID_PASSWORD unless emailPrivacyConfig.enableImprovedEmailPrivacy is set through its config route, which production no longer does by default

fireemuOnly.behaviour: codes are deterministic from the session seed rather than random

transient credentials are bounded: email action codes expire after an hour and phone codes after ten minutes of virtual time, pending second-factor sign-ins after an hour, and each kind refuses with QUOTA_EXCEEDED past 1000 outstanding codes per project or 32 pending sessions per user; the official emulator keeps every code until it is consumed and its pending credential is stateless (firebase-tools/lib/emulator/auth/state.js)

an admin batchCreate row whose passwordHash is not the emulator's fakeHash form creates the account without a password credential instead of storing an unverifiable hash; sign-in fails the same way on both sides

productionOnly: real identity provider round trips and provider-side account state

claims.statement: beforeCreate and beforeSignIn Blocking Functions run synchronously before an Auth commit for Auth stores in the Functions runtime's project; tenantId and the tenant resource are forwarded for tenant stores, registered projects without that runtime are isolated, explicit SDK error classes retain their canonical status, unhandled and seven-second transport failures return production-compatible 503 responses, every failure rolls the speculative operation back, and accepted userRecord and sessionClaims mutations are visible in committed users and newly issued tokens.
officialLimitations: firebase-tools 15.28.2 configures only beforeCreate and beforeSignIn in the Auth emulator; SDK email and SMS send hooks are production-only and are outside Local Emulator Suite parity

claims.statement: ID tokens are issued in the unsigned Firebase Auth Emulator format by default and are accepted only by the project of their audience.
officialLimitations: the Firebase Admin SDK accepts only alg none while FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST is set, so the firebase profile must sign with auth.idTokenSigning = unsigned-emulator

fireemuOnly.behaviour: auth.idTokenSigning = session-rsa issues RS256 tokens from a seed-derived key and publishes a JWKS, so every surface refuses unsigned or foreign-signed tokens

claims.statement: SMS second factors are enrolled, signed in with and withdrawn through the Identity Platform routes the official emulator serves, with the official eligibility refusals (first factor, verified email, duplicate number) and pending-credential shape. The official emulator's TOTP enrollment refusal is the default; declaring auth.totp explicitly enables fireemu's local TOTP extension.
officialLimitations: the official emulator sends no SMS: phone codes come from the emulator verificationCodes route
the official emulator refuses second-factor enrollment for an anonymous, phone, custom-token or Game Center first factor and for an unverified email

fireemuOnly.behaviour: declaring auth.totp enables local TOTP enrollment and sign-in; its acceptance window and enrolment session TTL are policies driven by the virtual clock, while an absent auth.totp preserves the official emulator's INVALID_ARGUMENT refusal
TOTP enrollment does not require a verified email: the official emulator has no TOTP route to measure it against and production behaviour is not inferred from the SMS result
default session snapshots carry no TOTP shared secret; a restore rebinds an enrolled factor to the secret the live store still holds and drops a factor whose secret is gone

surfaces.title: Cloud Storage for Firebase
surfaces.decision: Active supported surface. Parity is claimed for both dialects and for Storage Security Rules.
notes: import and export of the official Storage emulator artifacts are claimed by CLI-CLAIM-IMPORT-EXPORT under the cli surface (DATA-1 / DATA-2)

claims.statement: Both storage dialects the official emulator serves are reproduced: the Firebase protocol with resumable uploads and download tokens, and the JSON API with generation and metageneration preconditions, prefix / delimiter listing and range reads.
officialLimitations: the official Storage emulator implements no object versioning, no ACLs (its POST acl stub answers success without effect), no signed URLs, no compose and no notifications

the official Storage emulator parses no generation or metageneration precondition and verifies no declared checksum: it was measured to overwrite an object guarded by ifGenerationMatch=0, delete through a stale guard, and store a payload whose declared md5 did not match the bytes

the official Storage emulator ignores resumable offsets and the JSON API Content-Range chunk protocol: it appends whatever arrives and finalizes every PUT, so a two-chunk upload was measured to commit its first chunk as the whole object

the official Storage emulator registers JSON API object update (PATCH) and copy only on the short /b/... spelling: the /storage/v1/... spelling of those answers its 501 catch-all, and a bucket GET answers the 404 missing-object envelope; fireemu reproduces that route table exactly

a JSON API media insert without a name crashes the pinned official CLI outright (an unhandled TypeError after its own 400 exits firebase emulators:exec with code 2); fireemu answers a plain 400, and the row is recorded here because no fixture can record a crash

fireemuOnly.behaviour: a 256 MiB object cap, a 260 MiB body cap and a process-wide 1 GiB buffered-body budget answered with 503 and Retry-After

generation / metageneration preconditions, declared checksums, resumable offsets and the Content-Range chunk protocol are honoured as production honours them, refusing requests the official emulator admits (and corrupts state on); every such step is pinned as a documented divergence in conformance/storage-matrix.json

productionOnly: ACLs, signed URLs, object lifecycle management and Pub/Sub notifications

claims.statement: Storage Security Rules are evaluated on the Firebase dialect, at upload finalization against the received bytes, with firestore.get() and firestore.exists() available.
officialLimitations: the official emulator treats the whole JSON API as a privileged surface: Security Rules never run on it, whatever credential is presented (its adminStorageLayer validator answers true unconditionally), and fireemu reproduces that
the official emulator evaluates every upload as the rules create method, even over an existing object: a rule guarding update was measured to admit an anonymous overwrite
the official emulator's rules resource omits the production cacheControl and contentLanguage fields, so a rule reading them raises and denies there
the official rules runtime receives crc32c as a decimal string, not the base64 of the JSON API, and fireemu passes the same spelling
list requires rules_version 2 in the official rules runtime

a rules denial is answered with the fixed Permission denied. No READ|WRITE|LIST permission. envelope; the evaluation detail is a log line, and fireemu publishes its own through the control API instead

fireemuOnly.behaviour: an upload over an existing object evaluates the rules update method, as production evaluates it, so update-guarding rules keep working; the divergence from the official emulator's create-always is pinned in conformance/storage-matrix.json
resource.cacheControl and resource.contentLanguage are passed to Storage rules as production passes them

surfaces.title: Cloud Functions for Firebase
surfaces.decision: Active supported surface. Parity is claimed for HTTPS and callable functions, event triggers including Identity Platform Blocking Functions, Eventarc custom events and Firebase alerts, Cloud Tasks queue functions, scheduled functions, discovery over one or several codebases and the environment a runtime is started with, all running a real firebase-functions codebase in the bundled Node runner.
gaps: hot reload of a codebase's source

claims.statement: onRequest, onCall (v2) and v1 HTTPS functions run in the bundled Node runner behind /{project}/{region}/{function} and reproduce the official callable envelope, the two 404s of an unknown route, the timeout answer and the CORS a loopback origin gets. A v2 callable stream forwards sendChunk and onCallGenkit values progressively, keeps its final result pending until completion, and propagates a client disconnect to the runner while retaining admission for the stream lifetime.
officialLimitations: the official Functions emulator runs the runtime with token verification skipped, so any App Check field becomes an app with a null id and Bearer owner becomes an authenticated context with a null uid

the official emulator kills the runtime process of a function that overruns its timeout; it runs one process per trigger, and one fireemu runner serves a whole codebase, so fireemu answers the same 500 without taking the codebase down

fireemuOnly.behaviour: the daemon proxy refuses Bearer owner, forged bearer values and duplicate or folded auth fields as callable user identities instead of admitting them

a non-loopback Origin is refused with 403 instead of reflected; the official emulator runs its runtime with enableCors, so any page on the internet can drive a developer's local callable and read the result

claims.statement: v2 beforeUserCreated / beforeUserSignedIn and v1 auth.user().beforeCreate / beforeSignIn exports are discovered as served synchronous triggers and invoked by Auth through the guarded runner endpoint, which validates bounded canonical SDK failures and enforces the production seven-second deadline.
officialLimitations: firebase-tools 15.28.2 configures only beforeCreate and beforeSignIn in the Auth emulator; SDK email and SMS send hooks are production-only and are outside Local Emulator Suite parity

claims.statement: Firestore document, Storage object, Pub/Sub topic, Auth user, Eventarc custom and Firebase alert events are delivered to v1 and v2 handlers as JSON CloudEvents, and Cloud Tasks queue functions are enqueued through bounded per-queue FIFOs and dispatched under their declared rate and concurrency limits, all with retries, dead letters and bounded diagnostic retention. Queue statistics retain exact per-event timestamps and exclude a sample at the exact five-minute or one-minute boundary, matching the pinned emulator's strict greater-than comparison.
officialLimitations: the official emulator consumes JSON CloudEvents in the Node runtime; the protobuf payload form is not what firebase-functions reads

the official Tasks emulator ignores a task's scheduleTime -- nothing in its dispatch loop consults it, so a scheduled task fires immediately and the value only decorates the X-CloudTasks-TaskETA header

the official Tasks emulator starts every queue with zero tokens, refills once per second into a bucket whose capacity is max(maxDispatchesPerSecond, 1.1), holds maxConcurrentDispatches slots across retry backoff, and does not charge retry attempts to the rate bucket

fireemuOnly.behaviour: retries run on virtual-time backoff and awaitIdle replaces sleeping, and duplicate delivery is a seeded fault rather than an accident

the Eventarc publishEvents routes are served on the functions port rather than on the official suite's own Eventarc port, and CLOUD_EVENTARC_EMULATOR_HOST names that listener; an SDK reaches them unchanged
a task may not name a URL of its own: only this emulator's function URL is dispatched to, where the official emulator POSTs a task to any address it is given

the local runtime adds a process-wide ceiling of 10000 outstanding tasks and 64 MiB of retained task data, with completed duplicate-history queue and task names kept inside that byte budget and bounded to 65536 entries and 8 MiB of identifier text across all queues; the official emulator only bounds each pending FIFO to 10000 and otherwise retains completed names for the process lifetime

productionOnly: Cloud Tasks applies maxDispatchesPerSecond to every first or retry attempt; fireemu follows that production contract while the pinned Tasks emulator only consumes a token for the first attempt

claims.statement: onSchedule functions run against the virtual clock with cron and App Engine schedules, IANA time zones, a catch-up policy and an overlap policy.
officialLimitations: the official emulator does not run scheduled functions on a schedule at all: it exposes them for manual invocation

fireemuOnly.behaviour: scheduled runs are driven by the virtual clock, with scheduler.catchUp and scheduler.overlap deciding what a clock jump produces

claims.statement: Every export a codebase declares is accounted for: served, or named with the reason it is not, every codebase a firebase.json declares is loaded on a runner of its own, and SIGINT or SIGTERM shuts those runners and their descendants down cleanly.
officialLimitations: the official emulator never fails discovery on an unsupported export: it logs `Unsupported trigger` at DEBUG or `Unsupported function type on <name>` at WARN and records the definition with ignored: true, so a Realtime Database trigger in a suite without that emulator running is a line in the log and a handler that never fires

fireemuOnly.behaviour: an export whose trigger family belongs to a product fireemu does not serve fails discovery by default, naming every such function; functions.unservedTriggers = "report" asks for the official carry-on
a codebase whose declared runtime is not nodejs* is refused with the language named rather than handed to node

claims.statement: Under the firebase profile, a codebase inherits ordinary SCREAMING_SNAKE variables from the daemon process before its .env chain, .secret.local and .runtimeconfig.json are applied in the official order and dialect, while emulator-owned names and ambient Google credentials stay isolated; the strict profile isolates the entire parent environment, ordinary parameters resolve from the resulting runtime environment, and each local secret is exposed only to a function that declared it.
officialLimitations: the emulator resolves no parameters and prompts for nothing: a missing defineString is the empty string, a missing defineInt is 0, a missing defineList throws, and a declared default is a deploy-time value the runtime never sees
the pinned firebase-functions@7.3.2 has removed functions.config(), so CLOUD_RUNTIME_CONFIG is set and nothing in the supported SDK surface reads it

fireemuOnly.behaviour: a secret .secret.local does not carry stays unset; the official emulator falls back to Google Cloud Secret Manager, and fireemu holds no credentials and makes no network call

surfaces.title: Firebase App Check
surfaces.decision: A fireemu addition, not an official emulator: the pinned Local Emulator Suite ships no App Check surface at all. It is claimed on its own terms and can never be described as parity.
notes: the official emulators are the oracle for what they do not do: every enforced-denial row that would need a real project is recorded pending in conformance/DEBT.md

claims.statement: A local App Check issuer exchanges registered debug secrets for instance-signed RS256 tokens and publishes its public key at a JWKS route.

fireemuOnly.behaviour: the whole App Check surface: the official Local Emulator Suite ships no exchange endpoint, no JWKS route and no App Check verification, so this is an addition rather than parity
the private fireemu_epoch claim makes a local token deliberately non-portable across daemon instances

productionOnly: Play Integrity, App Attest, DeviceCheck and reCAPTCHA attestation, which prove device integrity and cannot be emulated

claims.statement: One transport-neutral admission decision governs off, unenforced and enforced modes for Auth, Firestore and Storage, and callable Functions enforcement is per function.
officialLimitations: the official emulators inspect X-Firebase-AppCheck on no product, so there is no oracle for an enforced denial and every such conformance row is recorded pending with the reason "needs a real project"

fireemuOnly.behaviour: an unverifiable or duplicated X-Firebase-AppCheck field is refused where the official Functions emulator admits it

productionOnly: the exact wire messages a real project returns under enforcement

claims.statement: Every classified request is recorded as a secret-free observation in a bounded per-project ring with cumulative counters, readable through the control API and the Emulator UI page.

fireemuOnly.behaviour: the observation surface has no official counterpart at all

claims.statement: The real firebase Web SDK obtains a local App Check token through initializeAppCheck with a CustomProvider and sends it to Firestore, Storage, Auth and a callable.

fireemuOnly.behaviour: @firebase/app-check hard-codes the production base URL, so the documented provider dials the local exchange itself

productionOnly: the Android, Apple and Flutter App Check SDKs, which are not exercised

claims.statement: Replay protection and production attestation providers are declared unsupported and fail closed rather than returning a token that proves nothing.
productionOnly: limited-use token issuance and atomic consumption, which need a real App Check backend

surfaces.title: fireemu control API (sessions, clock, snapshots, faults)
surfaces.decision: A fireemu addition with no official counterpart. It is the surface the deterministic features are driven through and is never described as emulator parity.

claims.statement: The control API owns project-scoped sessions, the virtual clock, snapshots, fault plans and awaitIdle; it has no official counterpart and is versioned on its own terms.

fireemuOnly.behaviour: session isolation by project, in-memory named snapshots with an all-or-nothing capture and restore, seeded fault plans, and awaitIdle instead of sleeping

productionOnly: nothing: this surface is deliberately test-only and has no production form

surfaces.title: Emulator Suite UI
surfaces.decision: Active supported surface with a scoped workflow claim. The fireemu UI covers the supported Auth, Firestore, Storage, Functions, Rules diagnostics and Firebase alerts journeys; the official UI v1.15.0 Logs browser boundary is separately verified against the Hub and the same Logging WebSocket. Android, Apple and Unity matrices and optional accessibility/visual snapshots remain outside this claim.
notes: the fireemu UI is an independent Solid application, so workflow parity is measured by reachable state and operation results rather than pixel identity
the official UI is a downloadable artifact (ui.main 1.15.0); its Logs page is verified through the Hub and fireemu's Logging WebSocket, while fireemu's own UI uses its bounded SSE log view
gaps: Android, Apple and Unity SDK/browser matrices
Realtime Database and Extensions remain deferred or not planned product surfaces

claims.statement: The fireemu UI supports the scoped active-product workflows for Auth, Firestore, Storage, Functions, Rules diagnostics and Firebase alerts, labels deferred and not-planned products, and exposes the same Hub-discovered Logging endpoint used by the official UI Logs browser journey.
officialLimitations: the official UI is a downloadable browser artifact and its visual layout is not a stable API contract

fireemuOnly.behaviour: the fireemu UI exposes deterministic runtime controls and a bounded SSE log view in addition to the scoped product workflows

surfaces.title: Firebase CLI configuration and command surface (firebase.json, --only, emulators:start / exec)
surfaces.decision: Active supported surface: the orchestration behaviour of firebase-tools 15.28.2 (configuration schema, service selection, environment export, command names, exit codes, the exec-only --ui opt-in, and the import / export artifacts) is reproduced for the served products; remaining gaps are listed explicitly.
gaps: an export carries the Firestore, Auth and Storage sections only: Realtime Database and SQL Connect are deferred products and their sections are refused rather than written

claims.statement: A firebase.json the official CLI accepts for the served products starts the same services on the same ports, --only decides which listeners exist and which canonical variables the command receives, unsupported official services are refused with their scope status, and the command names, flags and exit codes match firebase-tools 15.28.2.
officialLimitations: the official CLI only adds emulator variables to the child environment and never clears one it inherited

fireemuOnly.behaviour: variables of unselected services are cleared in the child environment, and GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT is set next to GCLOUD_PROJECT

emulators.<name>.host in firebase.json and bind in the canonical configuration accept only loopback (127.0.0.1, localhost, ::1); a routable host such as 0.0.0.0, :: or a LAN address, which firebase-tools 15.28.2 binds as given, exits 1 naming the key. The daemon serves without a credential on the products and its privileged control routes trust a loopback origin, so there is no routable mode; a suite that must be reached from another machine sits behind a reverse proxy that adds the credential. Runtime (crates/fireemu/src/config.rs loopback_host), corpus (spec/config/*invalid-examples) and tools/config-schema-check enforce one spelling set

claims.statement: An export directory firebase emulators:export wrote with firebase-tools 15.28.2 imports into fireemu with its Firestore documents, Auth accounts and Storage objects intact, and an export fireemu writes imports back into the official suite the same way: the firebase-export-metadata.json manifest, the Firestore managed export, the Identity Toolkit accounts and config documents and the Storage bucket, blob and metadata files are the pinned formats. --import, --export-on-exit and emulators:export behave as the official commands do, an import across products is all or nothing, and a section of a deferred product is refused rather than silently dropped.
officialLimitations: the Firestore managed export records no document creation or update time, so both suites stamp an imported document with the commit that installs it
the Auth emulator stores passwords in the clear (fakeHash:salt=<salt>:password=<plaintext>), so an export directory is equivalent to a password list
the official export request is hard-coded to databases/(default), so the format has no place for a named Firestore database
the official CLI overwrites a non-empty target directory once --force or --export-on-exit is given, whatever it holds

fireemuOnly.behaviour: an export directory and every file in it are created owner-only (0700 / 0600), because the Auth section carries password material
a directory is overwritten only when it is empty or already holds a firebase-export-metadata.json, whatever flags were given
Firestore databases other than (default) are written under a fireemu member of the manifest, which the official CLI ignores
a TOTP second factor, which the official Auth emulator has no equivalent for, is written under mfaInfo[].totpInfo.sharedSecretKey
a Storage blob id is derived from the bucket, object and generation instead of being a random UUID, so exporting the same state twice writes the same directory

surfaces.title: Emulator Hub
surfaces.decision: Active supported surface: the Emulator Hub serves discovery (GET /emulators in the official shape), the background-trigger switch and the locator file firebase-tools writes; the export trigger stays open until the import/export contract exists.
gaps: the export trigger the CLI drives through the hub (POST /_admin/export answers 501)

claims.statement: Official tooling discovers the running suite through the Emulator Hub on the official port without being told a host or port, and the hub's background-trigger switch drops events exactly like firebase-tools 15.28.2.
officialLimitations: the official hub notifies only the Functions emulator when triggers are disabled; other emulators keep posting events into 204 answers, so nothing is queued or replayed

fireemuOnly.behaviour: a loopback-Host guard on the hub routes (the official hub has none)

surfaces.title: Emulator logging
surfaces.decision: Active supported surface: an RFC 6455 WebSocket on the logging port serves the EmulatorLog wire format the official UI's Logs page reads, fed by the functions runner's output and the emulators' lifecycle lines; loopback-only and with a bounded history, both documented divergences.

claims.statement: The Logging emulator serves the EmulatorLog wire format of firebase-tools 15.28.2 over a WebSocket on the official logging port, preserves production Firebase Functions structured logger fields and severities, exports FIREBASE_LOGGING_EMULATOR_HOST and is discoverable through the Emulator Hub.
officialLimitations: the official transport keeps every log line in memory forever and serves the whole history to each new connection

fireemuOnly.behaviour: the WebSocket handshake is refused unless the Host header names loopback (the same DNS-rebinding guard the other fireemu listeners apply); the official server has none
the retained history is bounded to the most recent 1000 frames rather than unbounded, so an unbounded producer cannot exhaust memory

control-character stripping drops C0/C1/DEL and Unicode bidi-formatting controls from messages and structured field keys/string values as well as ANSI escape sequences, where Node's stripVTControlCharacters removes only the escape sequences; sanitized key collisions are retained under deterministic suffixes
function USER logs retain the severity documented for production Cloud Functions instead of being forced to info as the official emulator transport does
individual runner messages are truncated on a UTF-8 boundary at a conservative 256 KiB cap derived from Cloud Logging's approximate limit for the entire LogEntry

structured runner entries deeper than 64 levels or containing an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate are retained as bounded protocol-safe plain text rather than recursively decoded, and a user metadata field is nested under data.metadata.user whenever trusted attribution is present

surfaces.title: Cloud Pub/Sub
surfaces.decision: Active supported surface. The google.pubsub.v1 wire emulator is served over gRPC and REST/JSON on port 8085; parity is claimed for the documented subset the official Pub/Sub emulator implements.
notes: Pub/Sub snapshots (CreateSnapshot / GetSnapshot / ListSnapshots / ListTopicSnapshots / UpdateSnapshot / DeleteSnapshot and seek-to-snapshot) retain the source backlog and subsequent topic publications for replay into another same-topic subscription; lifetime is seven days minus the oldest unacknowledged message age and creation is refused below one remaining hour

push delivery is implemented for loopback HTTP endpoints with bounded workers, acknowledgement on 2xx, finite retry and nack on failure; remote, HTTPS and redirect endpoints are refused as a local safety boundary

REST/JSON transcoding on the Pub/Sub port implements the documented topic, subscription, snapshot, publish, pull, acknowledge, modify-ack-deadline and seek subset over the same broker state as gRPC; unsupported fields and update-mask paths are diagnosed explicitly

Avro/protobuf schema management and BigQuery / Cloud Storage subscription delivery remain outside the active implementation; the official emulator's documented unsupported delivery limitations are preserved

claims.statement: The google.pubsub.v1 wire emulator on port 8085 is served over gRPC and its documented REST/JSON subset: a real @google-cloud/pubsub or firebase-admin client creates, gets, lists and deletes topics and subscriptions, publishes, pulls (unary and streaming), acknowledges, extends and nacks ack deadlines, and seeks to a timestamp, with ordering keys, subscription filters and dead-letter forwarding; REST uses the annotated PUT resource routes and atomic FieldMask subscription updates; and a message published through the client protocol reaches subscribed onMessagePublished (v2) and topic().onPublish (v1) Cloud Functions only when the canonical source topic belongs to the Functions runtime project.
officialLimitations: the official Pub/Sub emulator supports no IAM operations
message retention is not configurable: all messages are retained indefinitely, and subscriptions do not expire
only Avro schemas are supported; protocol-buffer schemas are not
BigQuery and Cloud Storage subscriptions can be created but deliver nothing, and Single Message Transforms do not transform
UpdateTopic and UpdateSnapshot are not supported, and seek to a timestamp is not supported for ordered subscriptions

fireemuOnly.behaviour: ack deadlines and redelivery run on the virtual clock rather than wall-clock time, so a redelivery is deterministic and awaitIdle replaces sleeping; message ids and ack ids are reproducible under the daemon seed

a subscription seeked to a timestamp before a message was published replays that message even after it was acknowledged and even when retainAckedMessages is false; the official emulator replays it only when retainAckedMessages is set (conformance pubsub-probe/seek-to-time#replayed). A seek therefore never returns fewer messages than the official emulator

resource names, message attributes and ordering keys are rejected when they carry a NUL byte, which the official emulator admits; identifiers can never smuggle a NUL into a trace, a JSON document or a function payload

surfaces.title: Eventarc
surfaces.decision: Active supported surface. A configured Functions runtime starts a dedicated Eventarc listener on port 9299 and exports its URL to Functions codebases.

claims.statement: When a Functions codebase is loaded, the Eventarc support emulator has an independently bound listener advertised by the Hub and CLOUD_EVENTARC_EMULATOR_HOST; custom channel and google-channel publications are accepted only on that listener and dispatched through the live trigger table maintained by the official registration, removal and getTriggers routes.

fireemuOnly.behaviour: Eventarc trigger definitions are limited to 256 KiB after project substitution, the live registry to 4096 entries and 16 MiB including owned lookup and display indexes, one publish to 256 input events and 256 fault-expanded deliveries, and active Functions events to 4096 records and 64 MiB of serialized payload and routing data. Eventarc may consume at most 3072 records and 48 MiB, preserving a reservation for other trigger sources; admission fails atomically with 400, 413 or 429 rather than retaining unbounded local work.
fireemuOnly.reason: The production Eventarc control plane is managed and does not expose this local in-memory failure mode. The explicit bounds prevent a local SDK client from exhausting the emulator process.

fireemuOnly.behaviour: Custom Eventarc channels require the full project-qualified resource for dispatch, and Eventarc response CORS is restricted to loopback origins. OPTIONS is not synthesized and follows the pinned emulator's route miss behaviour.
fireemuOnly.reason: A local support listener must not become a cross-origin control plane for another project or a remote web page.

fireemuOnly.behaviour: Trigger removal compares parsed JSON objects semantically rather than preserving the pinned emulator's JSON member-order sensitivity.
fireemuOnly.reason: The production API represents a trigger definition as structured data, so member order is not a semantic distinction.

fireemuOnly.behaviour: A successful Functions source reload rebuilds the Eventarc table from the current manifest generation and removes manual, duplicate, or stale-generation registrations.
fireemuOnly.reason: The registration endpoints are emulator-local rather than a production Eventarc lifecycle API. Rebuilding prevents a stale local binding from dispatching after the source it named has been replaced.

surfaces.title: Cloud Tasks
surfaces.decision: Active supported surface. A configured Functions runtime starts a dedicated Cloud Tasks listener on port 9499 and exports its host to Functions codebases.

claims.statement: When a Functions codebase is loaded, the Cloud Tasks support emulator has an independently bound listener advertised by the Hub and CLOUD_TASKS_EMULATOR_HOST; queue creation and task enqueue routes are accepted only on that listener and feed matching task queue Functions.

surfaces.title: Firebase Data Connect
surfaces.decision: Deferred. The official Data Connect emulator is not a wire protocol fireemu can reimplement: it delegates to a Google-distributed toolkit binary that embeds a GraphQL engine over PostgreSQL/PGLite and generates SDKs. Reproducing that locally would mean either redistributing or downloading that Google binary -- which fireemu's distribution policy does not do -- or reimplementing a GraphQL-over-Postgres engine from scratch. Data Connect is also still a preview product. It is therefore deferred like Realtime Database, Hosting and App Hosting: nothing is served, --only dataconnect is refused with its deferred status, and a dataconnect_export section is refused on import.
notes: deferred by decision on 2026-08-31: depends on a Google-distributed GraphQL+Postgres toolkit binary that the no-download distribution policy will not ship, and the product is preview

surfaces.title: Firebase Realtime Database
surfaces.decision: Deferred for low expected near-term demand (2026-08-30 scope policy). It stays in the pinned baseline, so no complete-suite or unqualified superset claim may be made while it is deferred.

surfaces.title: Firebase Hosting
surfaces.decision: Deferred for low expected near-term demand (2026-08-30 scope policy). It stays in the pinned baseline.

surfaces.title: Firebase App Hosting
surfaces.decision: Deferred for low expected near-term demand (2026-08-30 scope policy). It stays in the pinned baseline.

surfaces.title: Firebase Extensions
surfaces.decision: Not planned: managed Firebase Extensions is deprecated and scheduled to shut down on 2027-03-31, so the product decision is to never implement it. It stays in the pinned baseline, so no complete-suite claim may be made against this baseline at all.
